column1: # scripts/verify/tests.tsv - regression manifest
# The bridge between doc/verification.md and tb/tests/. One line per runnable
# test; tab-separated; '#' starts a comment line.
#   T-id <TAB> uvm_test <TAB> wp <TAB> requirements <TAB> timeout_s <TAB> red
# T-id          must match the ID used in doc/verification.md (T-01, T-06, ...)
# uvm_test      the UVM test class name, i.e. tb/tests/<uvm_test>.sv
# wp            the work package that owns the test (0 = baseline / pilot)
# requirements  comma-separated FR-NN ids the test is evidence for, '-' if none
# timeout_s     hard wall-clock limit for one xsim run, in seconds
# red           mutant:<name>: the <name> row of scripts/verify/mutants.tsv reintroduces the defect
#               this test covers; the negative control rebuilds it and requires the test to fail
#               no: the test predates the flow; there is no mutant yet
# Optional 7th column, `sanity:<image>`: the test is the UVM sanity harness and
# runs a pre-built riscv-tests image. regress.cmake passes +HEX/+TOHOST (the
# tohost address is read from the ELF, never hardcoded) and requires both
# `UVM_RESULT: PASS` and `SANITY: PASS` in the log.
# Optional 7th column, `spike:<image>`: the same image, simulated twice -- in the
# DUT (+RETIRE_LOG) and in Spike -- and the two commit traces compared by commit
# index (scripts/verify/spike_trace.cmake, CTest label `spike`). regress.cmake
# does not declare these tests: the comparison is the test. The image is still
# built by the same `compile_sanity_<image>` target the `sanity:` spelling uses.
# A test listed here must exist in tb/tests/<uvm_test>.sv. After adding a line,
# re-run ./configure so CMake picks up the new sim_<uvm_test> target.
# wp 0 - baseline: the tests that existed before the work-package flow
# wp 14 F2 (E6): CSR file, Zicsr and trap entry. T-03 is the directed program:
# the six CSR* on mscratch, the rd=x0 / rs1=x0 clauses, one read per implemented
# address group plus one absent address, a write to mtval that must NOT trap
# (FR-52), and six traps back to back (ECALL 11, EBREAK 3, unallocated encoding
# 2, absent CSR 2, two writes to read-only addresses 2) honoured at the mtvec the
# program wrote. The oracle is the reference model (which derives the cause from
# the trapping instruction) plus the scoreboard, fed ONLY by the monitor's retire
# and trap streams. mtime and hart_id are driven non-zero (D13), so a DUT that
# reads zero for time/timeh/mhartid fails rather than passes.
# red=mutant:csr-illegal-noop is the planned row (wp-14 §5): a CSR access the
# configuration does not implement, and a write to a read-only address, must
# raise illegal-instruction instead of executing as a no-operation (FR-24,
# FR-47, FR-50). The catalogue row landed with the RTL text it mutates, as
# `store-grant-ignored` did for T-53. WP-14b batch 2a added five of the
# program's clauses as their own (T-03, mutant) pair: csr-write-always (D5),
# mepc-off-by-one (FR-23), misa-literal (FR-37), mhartid-zero (FR-32) and
# time-not-a-view (FR-49). The red cell therefore carries SIX names --
# csr-illegal-noop plus those five -- and not the seven this comment used to
# claim. Two further candidates were tried and removed in WP-14b:
#   trap-vector-fixed (FR-29) makes the program unrunnable: a wrong vector sends
#     the trap away from the program's handler, so the tohost store is never
#     reached, seq.start() never returns, and the only outcome is a CTest
#     wall-clock timeout with no UVM error -- the engine scores fail|timeout
#     only with a uvm_error, the rule that stops an OOM kill reading as a
#     defect. FR-29 is still observed by T-03's own pass (all six traps are
#     taken at the mtvec the program wrote), just not by a mutant.
#   trap-held-while-stalled (D12b) duplicated trap-valid-while-held on the same
#     rtl/control.sv line and was weaker (clk_en vs 1'b1); attached to T-03,
#     whose clk_en is always 1, it mutated nothing and passed. The arm belongs
#     to trap-valid-while-held, whose teeth are in T-62 (D12).
# wp 6 - store width, lane and strobes (FR-11). T-13/T-14/T-15 now carry their mutants (lane, halfword strobe, width cast) added with the catalogue rows in P4.
# wp 7 - RV32I closure (E4): one image per unstimulated instruction bin; every row carries its mutant (P3)
# T-37 is the local image scripts/verify/sanity/local/rv32ui-p-jalr_unaligned.S; every WP-7 row now carries its mutant
# wp 7 P4b - the last five acceptance-cell instructions get a named test each (bne, ori, slli, lui, auipc); the images already pass, the mutant is the proof
# wp 7 follow-up (FR-01): T-01 only ever issues ADD as `add x0,x0,x0`, so no test observed an ADD result. rv32ui-p-add
# checks one directly: TESTNUM 3 is `add rd,1,1` == 2, and `alu-ignore-rs2` makes it store 3. The mutant is shared
# with T-29..T-36; each row is applied independently (as branch-always-taken is for T-19..T-22 and T-38).
# wp 8 - retire observation and the monitor-fed model (G-28, C-16). T-44 runs T-01's program with the model fed
# by the monitor only (no program feed other than the monitor) and checks every published fetch pair against the
# program image (G-32) and the commit stream, per commit, against the same image (G-28). The mutant sends the
# bubble that follows a flush to write-back, so the commit stream is no longer the program.
# wp 8 follow-up (G-28): T-44's program is straight-line, so fetches == commits there and a model that counted
# fetches would pass it. T-45 runs a program whose taken forward branch skips two placed stores: 12 fetches, 10
# commits, difference 2 == the discarded fetches, and the two skipped PCs must never appear in the commit stream.
# wp 9 P1 (G-28 invariant): T-45's branch skips exactly the two words the front end
# lets go on a taken branch, so fetch-commit == |skip_pc| passed by coincidence. T-46
# skips three: 11 fetches, 9 commits, difference 2, and the checker must judge WHICH
# pc was fetched (0x0c/0x10 fetched and skipped, 0x14 never fetched), not a count.
# wp 9 (G-04): the Trace tests. Each row runs the same image twice -- in the DUT
# with +RETIRE_LOG and in Spike with --log-commits -- and compares the two commit
# traces instruction by instruction (pc, rd, value and encoding, by commit
# index). The 7th column is `spike:<image>`, not `sanity:<image>`: the test is the
# comparison, declared by scripts/verify/spike_trace.cmake, and regress.cmake
# deliberately does not declare it (a plain xsim row would assert nothing new).
# The images are the ones T-43/T-12/T-15 already simulate; the claim is new.
# What the comparison does NOT prove: a store writes no register, so its address
# and data are not in the trace. A mutant that changes only the store data path
# is invisible to the COMPARISON, not to the test: the test requires the DUT's
# own `^UVM_RESULT: PASS` as well (measured on `store-width-cast`: 31 UVM_ERRORs,
# trace 477/477 identical, test fails). The red cells below are the mutants that
# make the TRACES diverge, so the comparison itself is what catches them:
#   T-47 alu-ignore-rs2    -> count 47 vs 458, first divergence index 47
#   T-48 negative-branch    -> no_cut:dut, the trace never reaches <tohost>
#   T-49 store-lane-offset  -> count 52 vs 477, first divergence index 52
# wp 13 P1 (FR-11/FR-12/G-34): the halfword lane ignores addr[0] in both directions, so a
# LH/LHU at byte offset 1 takes bytes 0-1 and a SH at offset 1 strobes 0011 where 0110 is
# required. Offset 1 ONLY: a halfword at offset 3 spans bytes 3-4 and crosses the word, which
# is the split (FR-42/G-22, T-52) and belongs to P6. The mutant `halfword-lane-ignore-bit0`
# is two rows in `mutants.tsv` (load lane + store strobe), the halves the P2 fix repairs.
# wp 13 P3 (FR-38/G-18): the store does not wait for the data grant. Pre-fix,
# rtl/control.sv:288 gated the `data_ready` stall on the load destination, so a store drove
# its strobe for one cycle whatever the grant did (the fix is rtl/control.sv:294).
# T-53 configures the memory BFM to withhold the grant
# for two cycles (config_db, default 0 = today's behaviour) and riscv_small_store_grant_checker
# judges the monitor's per-access publication: a write that ended without a grant was
# accepted before it. The scoreboard is green in both worlds (address, strobes and data are
# right; the completion is not), which is why the claim has a protocol checker of its own.
# red=mutant:store-grant-ignored (wp 13 P4b) reverts the fix: it ties the store term of
# the stall condition to 1'b0, which is the pre-fix `!data_ready && mux_sel_rd_wb`. The
# fix's line cannot be the `find` itself because a cell may not carry `||` (mutants.tsv).
# wp 13 P5 (FR-42/G-22): the split. rv32ui-p-ma_data is the one image in the corpus
# with odd offsets; since P2's halfword lane it gets past cases 1-2 (`lh`/`lhu` at
# offset 1) and stops at MISALIGNED_LOAD_TEST(3, lw, s0, 1) -- the first WORD that
# crosses the word boundary, emitted today as one beat at the unaligned address.
# The verdict is the image's own tohost: no new TB class, the sanity checker judges.
# red=mutant:no-misaligned-split (P6) reverts the crossing detection, so the image is
# back to one beat at the unaligned address and reports testnum=3. The TB half of P6b
# (monitor beat index + strb checker low-bytes/high-bytes rule) is what turns the run
# green at the same RTL: before it, the image stored the pass value and the run still
# failed on 99 STRB_WIDTH errors from the partial beats.
# wp 14b (audit blockers 1/3/4 of wp-14 §16): the three arms WP-14 left unobserved
# or wrongly ordered, one test each. WP-14b batch 2a lands the catalogue row each
# red cell names; the recorded red log (build/regress/<run>/T-6x.log) at the
# RTL/TB digest that existed before the fix is the historical evidence, and the
# mutant below is the reproducible one (check 11).
# T-60: the model must execute the RETIRE of a cycle before the TRAP of the same
# cycle -- the retiring instruction is older (it is in WB, the trap in ID). The
# program reads `mepc`/`mcause` in the write-back slot of the trap's own cycle,
# so the pre-trap values must come back. Names FR-22/FR-23/FR-25.
# T-61: `exception[3:0]` reaches the DUT through the interface and the driver
# asserts it for one cycle on a scheduled instruction; the cause in `mcause` is
# the presented code (5, which no internal path produces), `mepc` is the aimed
# instruction, and its CSR write is discarded. Names FR-22 (`G-37`).
# T-62: D12 -- a trap raised while a crossing store holds MA (T-53's withholding
# memory): exactly one trap, taken on the release edge, and no instruction lost
# (image: the trap site must not retire, every other placed word must). Names
# wp 14b batch 2b (wp-14 §4.3, §18): the rv32mi images, built against the
# faithful env/p ceremony in scripts/verify/sanity/mi/riscv_test.h. The other
# sanity rows run an image whose verdict is a plain store; these run one whose
# verdict travels THROUGH the core's trap path: `_start` programs `mtvec` with
# `trap_vector`, the handler dispatches on `mcause`, and the `ECALL` inside
# RVTEST_PASS/RVTEST_FAIL reaches `write_tohost`, so `SANITY: PASS` is the
# image's own TESTNUM arriving via a trap. The environment is per-suite
# (`SANITY_SUITES`, `SANITY_IMAGES_rv32mi`); the three images below are the ones
# this WP claims and they pass. T-56 (rv32mi-p-illegal) and T-57
# (rv32mi-p-breakpoint) are deliberately NOT registered: they fail against the
# CORE, not the environment -- `illegal` needs MRET to return to `mepc` (FR-45,
# outside WP-14; the image hangs at pc=0x800003e4) and `breakpoint` needs the
# trigger CSRs (NUM_TRIGGERS = 0, FR-57 deferred; it stops at testnum=2). Their
# logs are build/sanity/rv32mi-p-illegal.log and -breakpoint.log.
# T-54: mcsr reads `misa` (XLEN), `mhartid` (== 0), `mimpid`/`marchid`/
# `mvendorid` and writes `mtvec`/`mepc`, all without trapping. red=csr-write-always
# is the D5 defect (a CSRRS with rs1=x0 that writes instead of suppressing):
# the read of a read-only identification register then traps.
# T-55: Zicntr through the four read-modify-write spellings on `cycle`/`instret`
# and their high halves, with rd=x0 and rs1/uimm=0 -- the reads must not trap.
# red is the same D5 defect, but through a different path than T-54's: it turns
# the first `csrr a0, mhartid` in reset_vector into a write, which traps BEFORE
# the program installs its handler (RISCV_MULTICORE_DISABLE precedes
# `csrw mtvec`, as in env/p). `mtvec` still holds its reset value 0, outside the
# image (linked at 0x8000_0000), and the memory BFM answers an out-of-program
# fetch with a NOP (riscv_small_driver.sv:274, NOP = 32'h33), so the PC walks up
# from 0 and the image's body never runs: the verdict is SANITY: TIMEOUT at the
# checker's cycle budget (measured pc=0x000c344c). That watchdog is independent
# of the sequence and raises a uvm_error, so check 11 scores it -- unlike the
# removed trap-vector-fixed, whose hang was inside seq.start(). It is NOT the
# image's own mtvec_handler, which is `j fail`. Installing the vector before the
# multicore block was rejected because it would not buy a FAIL either: the
# handler's RVTEST_FAIL spins while TESTNUM == 0, and the trap precedes
# `li TESTNUM, 0`, so the reorder would move the derailment without changing the
# verdict, and it would break the "env/p as published" contract this header
# exists for. The env/p order stays, and the narrative now says what the run
# actually does.
# T-58: the six Zicsr forms on `mscratch` (read-modify-write values, rd=x0 and
# rs1=x0 clauses) and the `misa` extension checks that decide the body's path.
# red=mutant:csrrc-and-instead-of-clear: `csrrc`/`csrrci` must CLEAR the bits
# rs1/uimm names; the mutant ANDs the source in instead, so the value the next
# `csrrsi a2, mscratch, 4` reads back disagrees at TESTNUM 4. `csr-write-always`
# is NOT this row's mutant -- every mscratch write it adds is legal, so the
# image passes on it -- which is why T-58 needed a catalogue row of its own
# rather than a borrowed one.
